title: Tooling: 2.49× faster production HPE audit via integer rows with identical receipts
body:
## Change and scope

At base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, production `research/complex-sw4-frame8/vendor/pr635/research/complex-571-cold14-st2/code/hpe_audit_and_transport.py` still stored every scalar row as a dictionary of `Fraction` values. Wronskode’s opt-in adapter `research/hpe-audit-fast-seed93/` already proved shared-denominator integer rows with identical layer-end control receipts. This PR wires that equivalent rewrite into the **production** PR635 auditor used by frontier1042 layer-end controls.

Other vendored `hpe_audit_and_transport.py` copies outside this PR635 path are intentionally left pairwise. Distinct from [#2357](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2357) (`hpe_audit_local.py`).

No certificate κ pins change. Same-tip provenance hygiene demotes previous live pins on this auditor to **provenance** (and drops them from live `VERIFY.json` inputs where applicable) in dependent packages including `k8-hpe450-binding`, `k8-hpe450-forward-audit`, `selected1094-extended-labels-seed65`, and `two-accumulator-saved-arms`. `frontier1042-lec-parallel` / `layer-end-controls-parallel` refresh production audit digests. The historical opt-in package vendors pairwise bytes as local `baseline.py`.

**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.** Selected frontier untouched.

## Result

On Linux / CPython 3.12.3 with `taskset -c 0`, five alternating fresh-process pairs timing the five honest FULL-WORD audits gave median wall time **6.304 → 2.528 s (2.49×)**. Timing is host-descriptive and is not a correctness gate. Every honest and seeded-fuzz outcome matches the pairwise baseline fieldwise (elapsed `seconds` excluded).

Package: `research/hpe-audit-integer-production/`.
Tip: `dbaf88ec7165ae8547d2756407583c04b3ead27b`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/hpe-audit-integer-production/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/hpe-audit-integer-production/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/hpe-audit-integer-production
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/k8-hpe450-binding --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/k8-hpe450-forward-audit --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected1094-extended-labels-seed65 --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-accumulator-saved-arms --check-only
python3.12 -B -m unittest tests.test_hpe_audit_integer_production
taskset -c 0 python3.12 -I -B research/hpe-audit-integer-production/benchmark.py --rounds 5
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_HPE_AUDIT_INTEGER_PRODUCTION assertions=26 honest=5 fuzz=40 corruption=receipt_divergence certs=0 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/hpe-audit-integer-production outcome=completed
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS
PASS_IDENTICAL_HPE_AUDIT_INTEGER_PRODUCTION_RECEIPTS
```

Default verify is read-only. Temp-copy apply-noop foil rejects via outcome divergence or runtime failure. Package gates under `-O` still launch asserting checker paths. Full `make verify`, selected cold replay, Lean, and multiplication-theorem obligations were not rerun for this isolated historical-checker change.

## Overlap and credit

Closest priors (different delivery): Wronskode’s `research/hpe-audit-fast-seed93/` (opt-in integer rows; this is the production wiring), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/756), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2357](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2357) (integer rows for `hpe_audit_local.py`, different object), LEC parallel schedulers (call scheduling without changing the audit kernel). No competing open PR on production PR635 `hpe_audit_and_transport.py` at refresh.

Credit Wronskode, icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds, and the retained PR635 lineage. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.
